chapter: Small group, new sound and Europe
title: Basie's stage presence and television manner
summary: They say Basie is natural on television and that he says little.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Was Basie presented, do you remember?
Well, Freddie, wouldn't you say that Basie -- during that time -- I mean he was polishing up his stage presence, wasn't he?
I mean, without maybe consciously doing it, but it was happening, wasn't it?
Because Stanley, I think you and I have remarked a number of times on the fact that Basie has developed -- I mean, he's got a good television personality by now.
Oh, yeah, yeah. He's something else.
The one thing that -- I think he should say more than he does, but -- (laugh) that's him, you know.
But, he can get away with it when --
Every now and again he comes -- you know -- when he does say something it's very witty.
Yeah, yeah. He doesn't get too far out there, you know.
And, one of the reasons that his personality is good for television, is that it's absolutely natural looking.
And, it is. He is just being his natural self.
And, it comes across that way.
It comes across to the audience -- the audience -- they realize what's going on, you know.
